sanskrit: tato 'haṃ punar evātha tān aṣṭau brahmavādinaḥ adrākṣaṃ dīpyamānān vai grahān aṣṭāv ivoditān
english: Then once more I beheld those eight expounders of the Veda, blazing like eight planets newly risen.

sanskrit: te māṃ sapraṇayaṃ vākyam abruvan samare sthitam praihi rāmaṃ mahābāho guruṃ lokahitaṃ kuru
english: With affection they spoke this word to me as I stood in the battle: 'Approach Rāma, O mighty-armed one; honor your teacher and act for the welfare of the worlds.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nivartitaṃ rāmaṃ suhṛdvākyena tena vai lokānāṃ ca hitaṃ kurvann aham apy ādade vacaḥ
english: Seeing that Rāma had been turned back by the words of his well-wishers, I too, acting for the welfare of the worlds, took up that counsel.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ rāmam āsādya vavande bhṛśavikṣataḥ rāmaś cābhyutsmayan premṇā mām uvāca mahātapāḥ
english: Then, sorely wounded, I came up to Rāma and saluted him; and Rāma, that great ascetic, smiling upon me with affection, said:

sanskrit: tvatsamo nāsti loke 'smin kṣatriyaḥ pṛthivīcaraḥ gamyatāṃ bhīṣma yuddhe 'smiṃs toṣito 'haṃ bhṛśaṃ tvayā
english: 'There is no warrior walking the earth equal to you in all this world. Go now, Bhīṣma; in this battle I have been greatly pleased by you.'

sanskrit: mama caiva samakṣaṃ tāṃ kanyām āhūya bhārgavaḥ uvāca dīnayā vācā madhye teṣāṃ tapasvinām
english: And in my very presence the descendant of Bhṛgu summoned that maiden and, in the midst of those ascetics, spoke to her in a sorrowful voice:

sanskrit: rāma uvāca pratyakṣam etal lokānāṃ sarveṣām eva bhāmini yathā mayā paraṃ śaktyā kṛtaṃ vai pauruṣaṃ mahat
english: Rāma said: It is plain before the eyes of all the worlds, O fair lady, how with my utmost might I have performed great feats of prowess.

sanskrit: na caiva yudhi śaknomi bhīṣmaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam viśeṣayitum atyartham uttamāstrāṇi darśayan
english: Yet even displaying my supreme weapons I am wholly unable in battle to gain the upper hand over Bhīṣma, the best of those who bear arms.

sanskrit: eṣā me paramā śaktir etan me paramaṃ balam yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ bhadre kim anyad vā karomi te
english: This is my utmost power, this my utmost strength. Go where you will, gentle one; what else can I do for you?

sanskrit: bhīṣmam eva prapadyasva na te 'nyā vidyate gatiḥ nirjito hy asmi bhīṣmeṇa mahāstrāṇi pramuñcatā
english: Turn to Bhīṣma himself for refuge; no other recourse is left to you. For I have been vanquished by Bhīṣma as he loosed his mighty weapons.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā tato rāmo viniḥśvasya mahāmanāḥ tūṣṇīm āsīt tadā kanyā provāca bhṛgunandanam
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, the high-souled Rāma sighed and fell silent; then the maiden addressed the delight of the Bhṛgus:

sanskrit: bhagavann evam evaitad yathāha bhagavāṃs tathā ajeyo yudhi bhīṣmo 'yam api devair udāradhīḥ
english: 'O blessed one, it is even so as your lordship has said: this Bhīṣma of noble mind is unconquerable in battle, even by the gods.'

sanskrit: yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ mama kāryaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā anidhāya raṇe vīryam astrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: 'You have done my work to the full measure of your power and zeal, withholding in the fight neither your valor nor your manifold weapons.'

sanskrit: na caiṣa śakyate yuddhe viśeṣayitum antataḥ na cāham enaṃ yāsyāmi punar bhīṣmaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: 'Yet in the end he cannot be overcome in battle; and never again, by any means, will I go to this Bhīṣma.'

sanskrit: gamiṣyāmi tu tatrāhaṃ yatra bhīṣmaṃ tapodhana samare pātayiṣyāmi svayam eva bhṛgūdvaha
english: 'But I shall go there, O treasury of austerity, whence I may myself fell Bhīṣma in battle, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā yayau kanyā roṣavyākulalocanā tapase dhṛtasaṃkalpā mama cintayatī vadham
english: Having spoken thus, the maiden departed, her eyes troubled with wrath, her resolve fixed upon austerity, brooding on my death.

sanskrit: tato mahendraṃ saha tair munibhir bhṛgusattamaḥ yathāgataṃ yayau rāmo mām upāmantrya bhārata
english: Then the best of the Bhṛgus, Rāma, together with those sages, took his leave of me and returned to Mahendra as he had come, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ ratham āruhya stūyamāno dvijātibhiḥ praviśya nagaraṃ mātre satyavatyai nyavedayam yathāvṛttaṃ mahārāja sā ca māṃ pratyanandata
english: Then, mounting my chariot and praised by the twice-born, I entered the city and reported to my mother Satyavatī all that had passed, O great king; and she rejoiced over me.

sanskrit: puruṣāṃś cādiśaṃ prājñān kanyāvṛttāntakarmaṇi divase divase hy asyā gatajalpitaceṣṭitam pratyāharaṃś ca me yuktāḥ sthitāḥ priyahite mama
english: And I appointed wise men to the task of watching the maiden's doings; day by day they, set diligently upon my good and welfare, reported to me her goings, her words, and her acts.

sanskrit: yadaiva hi vanaṃ prāyāt kanyā sā tapase dhṛtā tadaiva vyathito dīno gatacetā ivābhavam
english: From the very moment that maiden went to the forest, bent upon austerity, I became troubled and downcast, as though my senses had fled.

sanskrit: na hi māṃ kṣatriyaḥ kaś cid vīryeṇa vijayed yudhi ṛte brahmavidas tāta tapasā saṃśitavratāt
english: For no warrior could conquer me in battle by valor, my son, save one knowing the Veda, made keen by austerity and firm in his vow.

sanskrit: api caitan mayā rājan nārade 'pi niveditam vyāse caiva bhayāt kāryaṃ tau cobhau mām avocatām
english: And this too, O king, I disclosed out of fear to Nārada and to Vyāsa, that the deed might be averted; and both of them said to me:

sanskrit: na viṣādas tvayā kāryo bhīṣma kāśisutāṃ prati daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa ko nivartitum utsahet
english: 'You must not grieve, Bhīṣma, on account of the daughter of Kāśi. Who could venture by human effort to turn back fate?'

sanskrit: sā tu kanyā mahārāja praviśyāśramamaṇḍalam yamunātīram āśritya tapas tepe 'timānuṣam
english: But that maiden, O great king, entering the circle of hermitages and taking her stand on the bank of the Yamunā, practiced superhuman austerity.

sanskrit: nirāhārā kṛśā rūkṣā jaṭilā malapaṅkinī ṣaṇ māsān vāyubhakṣā ca sthāṇubhūtā tapodhanā
english: Without food, gaunt, withered, her hair matted, caked with dirt, that ascetic for six months lived on air alone, motionless as a post.

sanskrit: yamunātīram āsādya saṃvatsaram athāparam udavāsaṃ nirāhārā pārayām āsa bhāminī
english: Reaching the bank of the Yamunā, the fair lady passed yet another full year standing in the water, taking no food at all.

sanskrit: śīrṇaparṇena caikena pārayām āsa cāparam saṃvatsaraṃ tīvrakopā pādāṅguṣṭhāgradhiṣṭhitā
english: And, fierce in her wrath, she passed yet another year upon a single withered leaf, poised upon the tips of her toes.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi tāpayām āsa rodasī nivartyamānāpi tu sā jñātibhir naiva śakyate
english: Thus for twelve years she scorched heaven and earth; and though her kinsmen sought to turn her back, she could by no means be dissuaded.

sanskrit: tato 'gamad vatsabhūmiṃ siddhacāraṇasevitām āśramaṃ puṇyaśīlānāṃ tāpasānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Then she went to the land of the Vatsas, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, to the hermitage of the high-souled ascetics of holy conduct.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyeṣu deśeṣu sāplutāṅgī divāniśam vyacarat kāśikanyā sā yathākāmavicāriṇī
english: There, in those holy regions, the daughter of Kāśi, her limbs bathed in the sacred waters, wandered day and night, roaming at her own will.

sanskrit: nandāśrame mahārāja tatolūkāśrame śubhe cyavanasyāśrame caiva brahmaṇaḥ sthāna eva ca
english: At the hermitage of Nanda, O great king, and then at the fair hermitage of Ulūka, and at the hermitage of Cyavana, and at the abode of Brahmā;

sanskrit: prayāge devayajane devāraṇyeṣu caiva ha bhogavatyāṃ tathā rājan kauśikasyāśrame tathā
english: at Prayāga, the sacrificial ground of the gods, and in the forests of the gods, and in Bhogavatī, O king, and likewise at the hermitage of Kauśika;

sanskrit: māṇḍavyasyāśrame rājan dilīpasyāśrame tathā rāmahrade ca kauravya pailagārgyasya cāśrame
english: at the hermitage of Māṇḍavya, O king, and at the hermitage of Dilīpa, and at the pool of Rāma, O Kaurava, and at the hermitage of Paila and Gārgya—

sanskrit: eteṣu tīrtheṣu tadā kāśikanyā viśāṃ pate āplāvayata gātrāṇi tīvram āsthāya vai tapaḥ
english: in all these holy fords, O lord of peoples, did the daughter of Kāśi then bathe her limbs, undertaking the fiercest austerity.

sanskrit: tām abravīt kauraveya mama mātā jalotthitā kimarthaṃ kliśyase bhadre tathyam etad bravīhi me
english: My mother, O scion of Kuru, rising up from the water, said to her: 'Why do you torment yourself, gentle one? Tell me the truth of this.'

sanskrit: sainām athābravīd rājan kṛtāñjalir aninditā bhīṣmo rāmeṇa samare na jitaś cārulocane
english: Then she, the blameless one, with hands folded in reverence, answered her, O king: 'Bhīṣma was not conquered by Rāma in battle, O fair-eyed one.'

sanskrit: ko 'nyas tam utsahej jetum udyateṣuṃ mahīpatim sāhaṃ bhīṣmavināśāya tapas tapsye sudāruṇam
english: 'What other could venture to conquer that lord of earth with arrow raised? Therefore I shall practice the most terrible austerity for the destruction of Bhīṣma.'

sanskrit: carāmi pṛthivīṃ devi yathā hanyām ahaṃ nṛpam etad vrataphalaṃ dehe parasmin syād yathā hi me
english: 'I wander the earth, O goddess, that I may slay that king; let the fruit of this vow be mine in another body.'

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt sāgaragā jihmaṃ carasi bhāmini naiṣa kāmo 'navadyāṅgi śakyaḥ prāptuṃ tvayābale
english: Then the river that goes to the ocean said: 'You walk a crooked path, fair lady. This desire, O flawless of limb, you cannot attain, O weak one.'

sanskrit: yadi bhīṣmavināśāya kāśye carasi vai vratam vratasthā ca śarīraṃ tvaṃ yadi nāma vimokṣyasi nadī bhaviṣyasi śubhe kuṭilā vārṣikodakā
english: 'If, O daughter of Kāśi, you keep this vow for the destruction of Bhīṣma, and if while keeping the vow you shall give up your body, then you shall become a river, O fair one—crooked, watered only in the rains;'

sanskrit: dustīrthā cānabhijñeyā vārṣikī nāṣṭamāsikī bhīmagrāhavatī ghorā sarvabhūtabhayaṃkarī
english: 'hard to ford and trackless, flowing in the rains but dry the eight months, full of fearsome crocodiles, dreadful, a terror to all creatures.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājan kāśikanyāṃ nyavartata mātā mama mahābhāgā smayamāneva bhāminī
english: Having spoken thus to the daughter of Kāśi, O king, my illustrious mother, the fair lady, turned back as if smiling.

sanskrit: kadā cid aṣṭame māsi kadā cid daśame tathā na prāśnītodakam api punaḥ sā varavarṇinī
english: Sometimes in the eighth month, sometimes in the tenth, that maiden of fair complexion would again not so much as taste water.

sanskrit: sā vatsabhūmiṃ kauravya tīrthalobhāt tatas tataḥ patitā paridhāvantī punaḥ kāśipateḥ sutā
english: That daughter of the lord of Kāśi, O Kaurava, in her craving for holy fords, kept rushing here and there over the land of the Vatsas, again and again falling and running on.

sanskrit: sā nadī vatsabhūmyāṃ tu prathitāmbeti bhārata vārṣikī grāhabahulā dustīrthā kuṭilā tathā
english: And in the land of the Vatsas that river became renowned as Ambā, O Bhārata—watered in the rains, teeming with crocodiles, hard to ford, and winding.

sanskrit: sā kanyā tapasā tena bhāgārdhena vyajāyata nadī ca rājan vatseṣu kanyā caivābhavat tadā
english: By that austerity the maiden was born again from half of herself: she became both a river among the Vatsas, O king, and yet remained a maiden as well.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas te tāpasāḥ sarve tapase dhṛtaniścayām dṛṣṭvā nyavartayaṃs tāta kiṃ kāryam iti cābruvan
english: Bhīṣma said: Then all those ascetics, seeing her fixed in her resolve upon austerity, sought to turn her back, my son, and asked: 'What is your purpose?'

sanskrit: tān uvāca tataḥ kanyā tapovṛddhān ṛṣīṃs tadā nirākṛtāsmi bhīṣmeṇa bhraṃśitā patidharmataḥ
english: Then the maiden answered those seers grown old in austerity: 'I have been spurned by Bhīṣma, cast out from the estate of a wife.'

sanskrit: vadhārthaṃ tasya dīkṣā me na lokārthaṃ tapodhanāḥ nihatya bhīṣmaṃ gaccheyaṃ śāntim ity eva niścayaḥ
english: 'My vow is for his slaying, not for any heavenly world, O treasuries of austerity. When I have slain Bhīṣma I shall find peace—such is my resolve.'

sanskrit: yatkṛte duḥkhavasatim imāṃ prāptāsmi śāśvatīm patilokād vihīnā ca naiva strī na pumān iha
english: 'On whose account I have entered upon this everlasting abode of sorrow, bereft of the world of a husband, neither woman nor man am I here.'

sanskrit: nāhatvā yudhi gāṅgeyaṃ nivarteyaṃ tapodhanāḥ eṣa me hṛdi saṃkalpo yadartham idam udyatam
english: 'Without slaying the son of Gaṅgā in battle I shall not turn back, O treasuries of austerity. This is the resolve in my heart, the very end for which this effort is undertaken.'

sanskrit: strībhāve parinirviṇṇā puṃstvārthe kṛtaniścayā bhīṣme praticikīrṣāmi nāsmi vāryeti vai punaḥ
english: 'Wearied utterly of womanhood, resolved upon manhood, I would requite myself upon Bhīṣma; I am not to be turned aside'—so she said again.

sanskrit: tāṃ devo darśayām āsa śūlapāṇir umāpatiḥ madhye teṣāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ svena rūpeṇa bhāminīm
english: To that fair lady the god who bears the trident, the consort of Umā, showed himself in his own form, in the midst of those great seers.

sanskrit: chandyamānā vareṇātha sā vavre matparājayam vadhiṣyasīti tāṃ devaḥ pratyuvāca manasvinīm
english: Offered a boon, she chose my defeat; and the god answered that resolute woman: 'You shall slay him.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sā punar evātha kanyā rudram uvāca ha upapadyet kathaṃ deva striyo mama jayo yudhi strībhāvena ca me gāḍhaṃ manaḥ śāntam umāpate
english: Then once again the maiden spoke to Rudra: 'How, O god, can victory in battle be mine, a woman? And by my womanly nature my mind is wholly stilled, O consort of Umā.'

sanskrit: pratiśrutaś ca bhūteśa tvayā bhīṣmaparājayaḥ yathā sa satyo bhavati tathā kuru vṛṣadhvaja yathā hanyāṃ samāgamya bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ yudhi
english: 'The defeat of Bhīṣma has been promised by you, O lord of beings; so act, O bull-bannered one, that it may come true—that I, meeting Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu in battle, may slay him.'

sanskrit: tām uvāca mahādevaḥ kanyāṃ kila vṛṣadhvajaḥ na me vāg anṛtaṃ bhadre prāha satyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: To that maiden Mahādeva, the bull-bannered, replied: 'My word, gentle one, speaks no untruth; it shall come true.'

sanskrit: vadhiṣyasi raṇe bhīṣmaṃ puruṣatvaṃ ca lapsyase smariṣyasi ca tat sarvaṃ deham anyaṃ gatā satī
english: 'You shall slay Bhīṣma in battle and shall obtain manhood; and when you have passed into another body you shall remember all of this.'

sanskrit: drupadasya kule jātā bhaviṣyasi mahārathaḥ śīghrāstraś citrayodhī ca bhaviṣyasi susaṃmataḥ
english: 'Born in the line of Drupada, you shall become a great chariot-warrior; swift with weapons, skilled in varied modes of fighting, you shall become highly honored.'

sanskrit: yathoktam eva kalyāṇi sarvam etad bhaviṣyati bhaviṣyasi pumān paścāt kasmāc cit kālaparyayāt
english: 'Even as I have said, O blessed one, all this shall come to pass: in time, after some passing of the years, you shall become a man.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ kapardī vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ paśyatām eva viprāṇāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-splendored, matted-haired, bull-bannered god vanished then and there before the very eyes of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā paśyatāṃ teṣāṃ maharṣīṇām aninditā samāhṛtya vanāt tasmāt kāṣṭhāni varavarṇinī
english: Then, in the sight of those great seers, the blameless maiden of fair complexion gathered firewood from that forest;

sanskrit: citāṃ kṛtvā sumahatīṃ pradāya ca hutāśanam pradīpte 'gnau mahārāja roṣadīptena cetasā
english: and when she had built a great pyre and set fire to it, the flames blazing up, O great king, with a mind inflamed by wrath,

sanskrit: uktvā bhīṣmavadhāyeti praviveśa hutāśanam jyeṣṭhā kāśisutā rājan yamunām abhito nadīm
english: crying 'For the slaying of Bhīṣma!' the eldest daughter of Kāśi entered the fire, O king, beside the river Yamunā.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca kathaṃ śikhaṇḍī gāṅgeya kanyā bhūtvā satī tadā puruṣo 'bhavad yudhi śreṣṭha tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Duryodhana said: How, O son of Gaṅgā, did Śikhaṇḍin, having first been a maiden, become a man, O best in battle? Tell me that, grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca bhāryā tu tasya rājendra drupadasya mahīpateḥ mahiṣī dayitā hy āsīd aputrā ca viśāṃ pate
english: Bhīṣma said: The wife of that lord of earth Drupada, O king of kings, his beloved chief queen, was childless, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu drupado vai mahīpatiḥ apatyārthaṃ mahārāja toṣayām āsa śaṃkaram
english: At that very time the lord of earth Drupada, for the sake of offspring, O great king, propitiated Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: asmadvadhārthaṃ niścitya tapo ghoraṃ samāsthitaḥ lebhe kanyāṃ mahādevāt putro me syād iti bruvan
english: Resolved upon my destruction, he undertook terrible austerity and obtained from Mahādeva a daughter, though he had prayed, 'Let a son be mine.'

sanskrit: bhagavan putram icchāmi bhīṣmaṃ praticikīrṣayā ity ukto devadevena strīpumāṃs te bhaviṣyati
english: 'O blessed one, I desire a son, to requite myself upon Bhīṣma'—thus he spoke, and the god of gods replied: 'A woman-and-man shall be yours.'

sanskrit: nivartasva mahīpāla naitaj jātv anyathā bhavet sa tu gatvā ca nagaraṃ bhāryām idam uvāca ha
english: 'Turn back, O ruler of earth; this shall never be otherwise.' And he, going to the city, said this to his wife:

sanskrit: kṛto yatno mayā devi putrārthe tapasā mahān kanyā bhūtvā pumān bhāvī iti cokto 'smi śaṃbhunā
english: 'A great effort was made by me, O queen, through austerity, for the sake of a son; and I have been told by Śambhu, "Having been a maiden, it shall become a man."'

sanskrit: punaḥ punar yācyamāno diṣṭam ity abravīc chivaḥ na tad anyad dhi bhavitā bhavitavyaṃ hi tat tathā
english: 'Though entreated again and again, Śiva said only, "It is so destined"; for it shall be no otherwise—what must be will be even thus.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sā niyatā bhūtvā ṛtukāle manasvinī patnī drupadarājasya drupadaṃ saṃviveśa ha
english: Then that resolute woman, the wife of King Drupada, having purified herself, in her season approached Drupada.

sanskrit: lebhe garbhaṃ yathākālaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena hetunā pārṣatāt sā mahīpāla yathā māṃ nārado 'bravīt
english: In due time she conceived by the son of Pṛṣata, through the natural means ordained by rule, O ruler of earth, as Nārada told me.

sanskrit: tato dadhāra taṃ garbhaṃ devī rājīvalocanā tāṃ sa rājā priyāṃ bhāryāṃ drupadaḥ kurunandana putrasnehān mahābāhuḥ sukhaṃ paryacarat tadā
english: Then the lotus-eyed queen bore that child; and King Drupada, the mighty-armed, O delight of the Kurus, out of love for the child tended his dear wife with all comfort.

sanskrit: aputrasya tato rājño drupadasya mahīpateḥ kanyāṃ pravararūpāṃ tāṃ prājāyata narādhipa
english: Then to that sonless king Drupada, lord of earth, was born a daughter of surpassing beauty, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: aputrasya tu rājñaḥ sā drupadasya yaśasvinī khyāpayām āsa rājendra putro jāto mameti vai
english: But the illustrious wife of that sonless king Drupada gave it out, O king of kings: 'A son has been born to me.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā drupadaḥ pracchannāyā narādhipa putravat putrakāryāṇi sarvāṇi samakārayat
english: Then King Drupada, O ruler of men, had all the rites proper to a son performed for her, concealed as she was, as if for a son.

sanskrit: rakṣaṇaṃ caiva mantrasya mahiṣī drupadasya sā cakāra sarvayatnena bruvāṇā putra ity uta na hi tāṃ veda nagare kaś cid anyatra pārṣatāt
english: And the chief queen of Drupada guarded the secret with all care, declaring 'It is a son'; for none in the city knew the truth save the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: śraddadhāno hi tad vākyaṃ devasyādbhutatejasaḥ chādayām āsa tāṃ kanyāṃ pumān iti ca so 'bravīt
english: For, trusting in the word of the god of wondrous splendor, he concealed that daughter, and declared, 'It is a man.'
